---
engine: markdown
title: Your First Model
description: Predict whether a payment will be disputed, from its amount and merchant.
---

Start with one payment and one outcome: will this payment later be disputed?
You need Python 3.12 or newer. Install relflow in your project:

```bash
uv add relflow
```

## Describe One Payment

Each training record contains the information available at payment time and
the outcome observed later:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

## Define The Fields

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    batch_size=128,
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

`Number` represents the amount, `Category` represents the merchant, and
`Boolean` represents the yes-or-no outcome. `mask=True` marks `disputed` as
a prediction target: the model learns from its value without seeing it as
an input. `Model.xs` supplies a small model configuration.

```{typst}
//| label: fig-first-payment
//| fig-alt: "A payment has amount and merchant input fields, and a disputed Boolean prediction target."
//| fig-cap: "Two input fields support one prediction."
#tree(node("payment", kind: "root", children: (
  node("amount", type: "Number"),
  node("merchant", type: "Category"),
  node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean"),
)))
```

## Train The Model

Use your application's Parquet files, with one payment per row and the three
columns above. Train on earlier payments and validate on a later period;
both splits include the observed `disputed` labels.

```python
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

train_payments = pq.read_table("payments/train.parquet")
validation_payments = pq.read_table("payments/validation.parquet")

data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    train=train_payments,
    validate=validation_payments,
)
model.optimizer = rf.adamw(learning_rate=1e-3)
model.fit(data, max_epochs=20)
```

relflow configures the training loop, stops early when validation loss stops
improving, and restores the best validation checkpoint.

## Predict New Payments

The request table contains `amount` and `merchant`. It omits `disputed`,
because that is the outcome you want to predict.

```python
new_payments = pq.read_table("payments/requests.parquet")
predictions = model.predict(new_payments)
```

`predictions` is an Arrow table. Its `predictions` column contains the result
for `/disputed`; [Prediction Output](guides/prediction-output.qmd) explains how
to read its probability.

Next, [add transaction history](tutorials/transaction-history.qmd) to give
each payment more context. For training options and saving your model, see
[Training And Checkpoints](guides/lightning.qmd).
